back: A situation in which the free market misallocates resources, so output is not at the level that maximises the welfare of society.
People can use a non-excludable good without paying, so firms cannot charge and the good is under-provided.
One party to a transaction has more or better information than the other.
Taking more risk because someone else (such as an insurer) bears the cost.
Public goods, externalities, merit and demerit goods, information failure, monopoly power (also immobility, common property, inequality).

front: Why is a monopoly a source of market failure?
back: It restricts output and sets price above marginal cost, so P > MC and there is a welfare loss.

front: Why are primary product prices volatile?
back: Demand and supply are inelastic in the short run and supply varies with the weather, so small shifts cause large price changes.

front: What is the **tragedy of the commons**?
back: Over-use of a resource that nobody owns, because each user ignores the cost to others.
Limited information, cost, interest groups and unintended effects (government failure).
